newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MAVERICKS TRADE JASON KIDD TO SUNS IN SIX-PLAYER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MAVERICKS TRADE JASON KIDD TO SUNS IN SIX-PLAYER DEAL.

text.p: The Dallas Mavericks traded injured and disgruntled All-Star point guard Jason Kidd to the Phoenix Suns Thursday as part of a six-player deal.

The Mavericks acquired guard Sam Cassell and forwards Michael Finley and A.C. Green from the Suns. Phoenix, which also gave up a second-round draft pick in 1997 or 1998, acquired guard Tony Dumas and centre Loren Meyer.

Kidd was in Reunion Arena Thursday night in street clothes, sitting out his fourth straight game with a sprained ligament in the back of his neck. He said he learned of the trade just before the game against the Golden State Warriors.
"I had no sense of the trade or that I would be the one involved," Kidd said. "I'm excited about going to Phoenix to play with Kevin Johnson and his other buddies."
The 23-year-old Kidd was co-Rookie of the Year in 1995 and an All-Star in 1996. But he was unhappy with the deliberate playing style installed this season by new coach Jim Cleamons.

Kidd, who will make $4.4 million this season, feuded last year with backcourt mate Jimmy Jackson. The two said their troubles were behind them, but the team has struggled, going 9-16. Forward Jamal Mashburn also asked to be traded.

"The decision to make this trade, from a basketball perspective, was made by Jim Cleamons," Mavs minority owner Frank Zaccanelli said. "We see this deal as one which gives us multiple players who can help our franchise reach its goals."

Kidd's point guard spot will be filled by Cassell, who joins his third team in four months. Cassell joined the Suns in August as part of the deal that sent superstar Charles Barkley to the Houston Rockets. Cassell was leading the team with 14.8 points per game.

The 27-year-old Cassell was a 1993 first-round pick and helped the Rockets win back-to-back championships in his first two seasons. He will make $1.235 million this season and becomes a free agent July 1st.

The 23-year-old Finley had a superb rookie season in 1995-96, averaging 15 points per game and making the All-Rookie team. But he has fallen off this season, averaging 13 points and 4.4 rebounds. He will make $723,000 this season.

The Suns had made no secret of their desire to unload Green, who is 33 years old and will make $4.3 million this season. He won two NBA titles as a member of the Los Angeles Lakers and has played in 841 consecutive games, 65 short of the all-time mark. He is averaging 5.7 points and 5.1 rebounds.
Dumas and Meyer, both former first-round draft picks, have not played much this season and were included to balance the deal for salary cap purposes.
Dumas, who will make $1.1 million, is sidelined with a broken finger. He is averaging four points per game. Meyer, who will make $639,000, is averaging 4.1 points and 2.6 rebounds.

It has been a year of major change for the Suns, who have had three coaches in the last 12 months. They have been involved in the NBA's two biggest trades since the end of last season -- the Barkley deal and this one.
Phoenix lost its first 13 games this season and replaced coach Cotton Fitzsimmons with Danny Ainge during the slide. The Suns are 8-11 since Ainge took over.
